$comment: TypeScript is enabled INCREMENTALLY, not by a big-bang rewrite.
`allowJs: true` + `checkJs: false` means the 62 existing .js/.jsx files keep
working untouched and untypechecked, while every new file is .ts/.tsx and is
checked at full strictness. A 62-file rewrite done in one pass would be a huge
unreviewable diff across a codebase whose token engine is finished and heavily
commented — and it would buy nothing that migrating file-by-file does not.
Vite transpiles TS with esbuild and does NOT typecheck, so `npm run build`
cannot be broken by a type error. Typechecking is its own gate: `npm run
typecheck`. That separation is deliberate — a type error should fail CI, not
the dev server someone is using to look at a screen.
TypeScript 7 removed `baseUrl`; `paths` now resolves relative to this file.
